title: Warren Buffett's $35 Billion Bet on Tim Cook's Apple Grew to $185 Billion Pretax. Here's What That Stake Says About Long-Term Investing.
author: Dave Kovaleski
description: Berkshire Hathaway's $35 billion investment in Apple made in 2016 has grown to $185 billion pretax over 10 years, becoming the company's largest holding. The investment exemplifies Buffett's investing philosophy of buying great businesses at fair prices, backing strong leadership, and maintaining long-term positions. Apple peaked at 50% of Berkshire's portfolio in 2023 but has since been reduced to 22% as Buffett took profits and diversified.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Apple is portrayed as Buffett's best investment, with a $35 billion initial stake growing to $185 billion pretax. Described as having strong leadership, industry dominance, and a competitive moat, making it the perfect Buffett investment exemplifying long-term value creation.

IBM is mentioned only as a historical reference point (2011 investment) marking Buffett's initial foray into technology stocks. No performance data or current sentiment is provided about this position.

Berkshire's strategic Apple investment demonstrates successful capital allocation and long-term investing discipline. The company's ability to generate $185 billion in pretax gains from a $35 billion investment showcases effective portfolio management and shareholder value creation.

title: IBM Software Growth Slows: Will Recurring Revenue Support Recovery?
author: Na
description: IBM's Software segment revenues grew 5% to $7.8 billion in Q2 2026, but organic growth was flat due to customers shifting spending toward infrastructure. However, Hybrid Cloud revenues grew 11% with OpenShift ARR reaching $2.2 billion, and the Data business surged 19%. Despite revenue headwinds, IBM expanded Software segment profit by 9% to $2.5 billion with margin expansion of 110 basis points.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Mixed results with flat organic growth in Software offset by strong margin expansion (110 bps), Hybrid Cloud growth (11%), and Data business surge (19%). However, Transaction Processing declined 8% and overall Software organic growth was flat, indicating near-term headwinds despite profitability improvements.

Productivity & Business Processes segment grew 14% YoY to $37.8 billion, with Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenues up 14-16%, demonstrating strong competitive positioning against IBM in cloud and productivity software.

Cloud revenues (SaaS + IaaS) surged 47% in USD to $9.9 billion, showing cloud as the primary growth driver. However, overall Software revenues declined 2% as customers migrate from on-premises to cloud.

title: IBM (IBM) Sees a More Significant Dip Than Broader Market: Some Facts to Know
author: Zacks.Com
description: IBM stock fell 4.38% on September 16, 2026, underperforming the broader market. The company is expected to report earnings on October 21, 2026, with projected EPS growth of 9.06% and revenue growth of 3.34% year-over-year. IBM currently holds a Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold) with a Forward P/E ratio of 20.15, trading at a discount to its industry average.

However, the Zacks Rank of #3 (Hold) and minimal change in consensus EPS estimates (-0.01%) suggest a neutral outlook in the near term.
